reason: This passage (Exodus 3:1-18) describes God's call to Moses at the burning bush. The text contains no interaction between Moses and the Israelite people, and no depiction of antagonism toward any leader. While the passage mentions the 'cry of the children of Israel' (צַעֲקַ֥ת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) referring to their suffering under Egyptian oppression, it does not describe antagonism toward a leader. At this narrative point, Moses has not yet been established as a leader of the people—he is being commissioned by God for that role. The entire passage focuses on God's communication with Moses about his divine mission.
